primary_sources.title: Conjectures on the Critical Points of a Polynomial
primary_sources.author: Morris Marden
primary_sources.exact_anchor: pp. 267--268: Gauss--Lucas, Sendov's root-to-critical unit-distance question, and the inverse-distance equilibrium interpretation.
primary_sources.supports: The classical unit-disk localization setting and reciprocal-force interpretation.
primary_sources.does_not_support: A theorem fixing a critical point and bounding the sum of its two nearest root distances.

primary_sources.supports: The modern nearby landscape: root-to-critical distance products and one-root exclusion geometry derived from reciprocal balance.

primary_sources.title: The zeros of a polynomial
primary_sources.author: J. H. Grace
primary_sources.venue: Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 11 (1902), 352--357
primary_sources.exact_anchor: The classical two-zero localization theorem, conventionally restated as locating a derivative zero in an explicit disk determined by two zeros.
primary_sources.supports: The closest classical theorem involving two zeros and one critical point.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The reverse input direction or the sum of the two nearest root distances from every critical point.

supporting_survey.title: Critical points of polynomials
supporting_survey.author: Vilmos Totik
supporting_survey.exact_anchor: Theorem 14 (Grace), Theorem 15 (Walsh), and Theorem 16 plus its corollary (Dimitrov), in the circular-domains section.
supporting_survey.use: Confirms the conventional directions and terminology of the closest classical localization results; it is not used as novelty authority.

mechanism_comparison.grace_heawood: Input: two prescribed zeros. Output: existence of a critical point in a disk determined by them.
mechanism_comparison.sendov_marden: Input: one prescribed zero of a unit-disk polynomial. Output sought: a critical point within unit distance.
mechanism_comparison.alexander_walsh: Input: one prescribed zero and its separation from the other zeros. Output: an exclusion disk containing no nontrivial critical point.
mechanism_comparison.local_theorem: Input: one prescribed critical point of a unit-disk polynomial. Output: its two nearest roots have total distance at most two.
mechanism_comparison.geometric_mean_scale_interface: The Lean-checked conditional theorem gives two distinct roots with total distance at most twice the positive geometric mean of the root distances. It is a local scale interface within the same metric mechanism; the global theorem adds disk geometry to obtain the absolute diameter bound.
mechanism_comparison.exact_delta: The quantifier direction and paired sum conclusion are distinct from all three located families. The proof nevertheless uses classical logarithmic-derivative equilibrium and elementary disk geometry.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: The theorem is metric only. It does not make the root-to-hub segments or any replacement path lie in the unit lemniscate.
